shippingNews.postTitle: BBC Philippines LNG Tanks Successfully Unloaded at Sturgeon Bay

stories.body: STURGEON BAY, WI – The 482-foot-long heavy lift vessel BBC Philippines departed Sturgeon Bay Monday for Burns Harbor after finishing unloading four huge Liquid Natural Gas (LNG) tanks. The tanks are for the new build 3794, a bunkering barge being built at Bay Shipbuilding that will be used to fuel ships at sea. Each thank had to be individually barged from the ship, anchored out in the bay, to the shipyard. Basic Marine’s tug Nickelena powered the barge with assistance from the smaller tug Krystal. shippingNews.postTitle: Iron Ore, Steel Shipments Decline at Great Lakes Ports Due in Part to Trump Tariffs

stories.body: Great Lakes ports are seeing declines in iron ore and steel shipments that are tied in part to the ongoing trade dispute between the U.S. and Canada. In August, President Donald Trump imposed 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, including alcohol, dairy products and motor vehicles. Canada responded on Sept. 8 with about $20 billion of its own retaliatory tariffs that include steel, agricultural equipment and pulp and paper products. todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: A 30.2 inch high pressure centered over central Ontario continues to moves east into Quebec by this afternoon. Meanwhile, a 29.9 inch low is moving into Manitoba, and another 29.9 inch low is developing over the southern Plains. This afternoon, the lows begin to converge over the Upper Midwest, consolidating into a 29.8 inch low near Chicago this evening and moving northeast into the LP tonight. In its wake, a 30.9 inch high builds over Wyoming, weakening to 30.6 inches Friday as it expands over the Plains while the low deepens to 29.5 inches and heads towards New England. The high slides south of the Great Lakes at 30.4 inches by Saturday night as a 29.4 inch Alberta Clipper moves into Saskatchewan. Sunday, the high builds back to 30.5 inches over the Delmarva Peninsula as the Clipper moves into Manitoba. Ridging recovers over the Great Lakes Monday.

marineWeather.synopsis: Winds will gradually become easterly tonight as high pressure around 30.3 inches slides through the region. The stronger winds are expected across the southern half of the lake during this time. Two areas of low pressure are progged to merge over the Great Lakes region into a single low pressure tonight and deepen to around 29.5 inches as it shifts into the eastern Great Lakes through Friday. Expect a northwesterly wind shift to ramp up and increase to gales and nearing storm force at times on the backside of the departing low pressure while a strong high pressure around 30.7 inches builds to the west. A Gale Warning is now in effect for all of the open waters of Lake Michigan Friday morning into Friday night. Widespread rain is expected this afternoon into tonight, with a few thunderstorms possible over the southern open waters. Lake effect showers & thundershowers may linger into Friday along the back side of departing low pressure. A few waterspouts are possible in the Friday showers/thundershowers, particularly over the southern half of Lake Michigan. A strong cold front in its wake brings likely northerly gales late Friday.

marineWeather.synopsis: High pressure 30.10 inches builds off to the east of Lake Erie through the afternoon. A warm front will lift north across the lake late this evening as low pressure 29.60 inches moves into the Great Lakes. A cold front will sweep across the lake early Friday with high pressure 30.50 inches building into the Ohio Valley this weekend.

A 30.4 inch high will drift east across Quebec and New England through tonight. A 29.5 inch low will then move from southern lower Michigan tonight to just north of the lake Friday morning before reaching the Saint Lawrence Valley by late Friday afternoon. This low will deepen to 29.1 inches as it moves from the Saint Lawrence Valley Friday night to the Canadian Maritimes Saturday. A strong and broad 30.6 inch high is then forecast to build from the Ohio Valley Saturday night to the Mid Atlantic and southern New England by Sunday night before drifting south of the Canadian Maritimes Monday.
